images.title: Trap the root of 1936
images.purpose: Shows the square root of 1936 trapped between 40 and 50, narrowed to 44 or 46 by the last digit, and fixed at 44 because 45 squared is too big.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One number line across the centre with ten unit gaps and a few marked points.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal number line from 40 to 50 with exactly 11 evenly spaced ticks. The left end tick is labelled 40² = 1600 and the right end tick 50² = 2500. Ticks 44 and 46 carry amber (#E69F00) dots labelled 44 and 46. Tick 45 carries a short grey (#6B7280) vertical bar labelled 45. The 44 dot has a reddish purple (#CC79A7) ring around it. Above the line, centred: √1936 = 44. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Nearby squares trap the root, and the last digit picks between two choices.
images.description: Shows the square root of 1936 trapped between 40 and 50, narrowed to 44 or 46 by the last digit, and fixed at 44 because 45 squared is too big.
images.context: 1936 ends in 6, so the root ends in 4 or 6; 45² = 2025 > 1936.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the two candidates and the 45 divider on one line makes the estimation steps easy to follow.
